sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And next up, we have Diana shouting out to the Polanski unit.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们听听黛安娜向波兰斯基监区大声喊话。

sentences.en: Hito, it's Mama D.
sentences.zh: 希托，我是D妈妈。

sentences.en: I know I sound kind of different.
sentences.zh: 我知道我的声音听起来有点不一样。

sentences.en: I'm very sick right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在病得很重。

sentences.en: I got diagnosed with pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 我被诊断出得了肺炎。

sentences.en: I've been sick already for quite some time now.
sentences.zh: 我已经病了相当长一段时间了。

sentences.en: This is the voice of a woman calling into a radio show on the Texas station KPFA.
sentences.zh: 这是一个女人打给德克萨斯州KPFA电台节目的声音。

sentences.en: She has a personal message for a prison in me.
sentences.zh: 她有一条发给监狱里某人的个人信息。

sentences.en: Anyway, I want to tell you, Hito, that Mama D.
sentences.zh: 总之，我想告诉你，希托，D妈妈

sentences.en: loves you.
sentences.zh: 爱着你。

sentences.en: I always think of you.
sentences.zh: 我总是想起你。

sentences.en: And it's just getting harder and harder.
sentences.zh: 而且情况变得越来越艰难。

sentences.en: I know I'm not supposed to cry because you're going to get mad at me,
sentences.zh: 我知道我不该哭，因为你会生我的气，

sentences.en: but I can't help but feel so much love for you.
sentences.zh: 但我还是忍不住对你充满爱意。

sentences.en: Calling into a program like this is one of the few ways for spouses and parents and children
sentences.zh: 打这样的节目电话是配偶、父母和孩子与囚犯沟通的少数几种方式之一，

sentences.en: to communicate with prisoners, especially inmates in solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于被单独监禁的囚犯。

sentences.en: Many prisoners in solitary have been found guilty of heinous crimes, including murder,
sentences.zh: 许多被单独监禁的囚犯都被判定犯有滔天罪行，包括谋杀、

sentences.en: rape, terrorism.
sentences.zh: 强奸、恐怖主义。

sentences.en: But here's something you might not know.
sentences.zh: 但有些事你可能不知道。

sentences.en: Some are there because they're difficult to manage or because of bureaucratic inertia.
sentences.zh: 有些人被关在那里是因为他们难以管教，或者由于官僚机构的因循守旧。

sentences.en: While judges and juries decide whether someone should go to prison,
sentences.zh: 虽然法官和陪审团决定某人是否应该入狱，

sentences.en: a decision that can be appealed in court,
sentences.zh: 这是一个可以在法庭上上诉的决定，

sentences.en: typically it's prison officials who decide whether someone should be in solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 但通常是由监狱官员来决定某人是否应该被单独监禁。

sentences.en: In recent years, both liberals and conservatives worried about the psychological and financial costs
sentences.zh: 近年来，自由派和保守派都对长期单独监禁的心理成本和财务成本感到担忧，

sentences.en: of long-term solitary confinement have raised questions about the practice.
sentences.zh: 并对这种做法提出了质疑。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we thought we'd take a look at what happens inside the prison cells
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》中，我们想带大家看看鲜有人能见到的监狱牢房内部发生了什么，

sentences.en: that few people ever see and the psychological effects of being alone for long periods of time.
sentences.zh: 以及长期独处带来的心理影响。

sentences.en: Karamit Ryder is a professor of criminology at the University of California, Irvine,
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特·赖德是加州大学尔湾分校的犯罪学教授，

sentences.en: and the author of the new book, 23-7, Pelican Bay Prison and the Rise of Long-Term Solitary Confinement.
sentences.zh: 也是新书《23-7：鹈鹕湾监狱与长期单独监禁的兴起》的作者。

sentences.en: Besides being a researcher, she's also been a prisoners' rights activist at Human Rights Watch.
sentences.zh: 除了研究人员，她还曾担任“人权观察”组织的囚犯权益活动家。

sentences.en: Karamit, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: You can't tell the story of solitary confinement without understanding the story of a man named George Jackson.
sentences.zh: 如果不了解乔治·杰克逊这个人的故事，你就无法讲述单独监禁的故事。

sentences.en: He was sent to prison in the early 1960s after pleading guilty to armed robbery,
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪60年代初因承认武装抢劫罪而被送进监狱，

sentences.en: and he was sentenced to a term of one year to life.
sentences.zh: 并被判处一年至无期徒刑。

sentences.en: What was the thinking behind this kind of indeterminate sentence?
sentences.zh: 这种不定期刑期背后的考量是什么？

sentences.en: So the idea for someone like George Jackson was that he would go to prison
sentences.zh: 所以，对于乔治·杰克逊这样的人来说，他的想法是他会进入监狱，

sentences.en: and he'd have to prove that he'd been rehabilitated before he could get out of prison.
sentences.zh: 他必须证明自己已经改过自新，然后才能出狱。

sentences.en: Around the time Jackson went to prison, however,
sentences.zh: 然而，在大约杰克逊入狱的时期，

sentences.en: people started to look at these indeterminate sentences
sentences.zh: 人们开始审视这些不定期刑期，

sentences.en: and realize that they were having truly disproportionate impacts
sentences.zh: 并意识到它们产生了极其不成比例的影响，

sentences.en: depending on the race of the person with the sentence.
sentences.zh: 这取决于服刑人员的种族。

sentences.en: So white people had a much easier time convincing prison officials
sentences.zh: 因此，白人要比像乔治·杰克逊这样的非裔美国男性

sentences.en: that they had been reformed and should be let out of prison
sentences.zh: 更容易说服监狱官员

sentences.en: than African-American men like George Jackson happened to be.
sentences.zh: 他们已经改过自新并应该被释放。

sentences.en: So George Jackson found himself essentially stuck in prison.
sentences.zh: 所以乔治·杰克逊发现自己基本上被困在了监狱里。

sentences.en: Years went by when he was denied parole, and he became radicalized in this process.
sentences.zh: 多年过去了，他的假释申请一直被拒，在这个过程中他变得激进起来。

sentences.en: He wrote a book of best-selling letters that achieved national and international acclaim,
sentences.zh: 他写了一本畅销书信集，在国内外获得了高度赞誉，

sentences.en: letters to his family and to his lawyers articulating his revolutionary politics
sentences.zh: 信是写给他的家人和律师的，阐述了他的革命政治观点

sentences.en: and the problems with things like this indeterminate sentence.
sentences.zh: 以及诸如此类的不定期刑期所存在的问题。

sentences.en: This brought him to the attention of prison officials,
sentences.zh: 这引起了监狱官员的注意，

sentences.en: and he was accused of murdering a prison guard in the early 1970s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代初，他被指控谋杀了一名狱警。

sentences.en: And he was preemptively sent to death row at San Quentin
sentences.zh: 他被先发制人地送往圣昆廷监狱的死囚牢房，

sentences.en: while he awaited a death penalty trial for that murder he was accused of.
sentences.zh: 同时等待因被指控谋杀而面临的死刑审判。

sentences.en: And while on death row at San Quentin, in an isolation unit, interestingly,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当他在圣昆廷监狱死囚牢房的一个隔离区时，

sentences.en: one day his lawyer came in to visit him.
sentences.zh: 有一天他的律师来探望他。

sentences.en: And the story that prison officials tell, and it's been repeated many times,
sentences.zh: 监狱官员讲述并被多次重复的故事是，

sentences.en: is that his lawyer snuck a 9-millimeter gun into him inside of a tape recorder,
sentences.zh: 他的律师把一把9毫米手枪藏在录音机里带给了他，

sentences.en: and that Jackson then used that gun to try to escape from this isolation unit.
sentences.zh: 然后杰克逊用那把枪试图逃离这个隔离区。

sentences.en: All we actually know is that he was shot to death on the San Quentin prison yard
sentences.zh: 我们实际知道的全部就是，当他跑出隔离区时，

sentences.en: as he ran out of the isolation unit.
sentences.zh: 他在圣昆廷监狱的操场上被枪击身亡。

sentences.en: And when staff ran into the unit to see what had happened,
sentences.zh: 当工作人员冲进隔离区查看发生了什么时，

sentences.en: they found three officers and two more prisoners who'd been stabbed to death.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了三名警官和另外两名被刺身亡的囚犯。

sentences.en: So this was the most violent day in California's prison history ever,
sentences.zh: 所以这是加州监狱史上最暴力的一天，

sentences.en: six deaths total on August 21st, 1971.
sentences.zh: 1971年8月21日总共六人死亡。

sentences.en: And this moment is a moment that people point to in California
sentences.zh: 人们认为加州的这一时刻

sentences.en: as incredibly important in understanding why the state needed long-term solitary confinement units.
sentences.zh: 对于理解为什么该州需要长期单独监禁区至关重要。

sentences.en: And similar things happened across the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 美国各地也发生过类似的事情，

sentences.en: and prison officials in other states point to those moments.
sentences.zh: 其他州的监狱官员也以这些时刻为例。

sentences.en: So two weeks after George Jackson died, the revolt at Attica happened.
sentences.zh: 因此，在乔治·杰克逊死后两周，阿提卡监狱暴动发生了。

sentences.en: Similarly, following that, prisoners were locked into their cells,
sentences.zh: 同样，在那之后，囚犯们被锁在牢房里，

sentences.en: and that became a moment people pointed to as a justification
sentences.zh: 这成为了人们用来为

sentences.en: for really long-term solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 真正长期的单独监禁辩护的一个时刻。

sentences.en: You also tell the story of a prison administrator, Carl Larson,
sentences.zh: 你还讲述了一位监狱管理者卡尔·拉尔森的故事，

sentences.en: who began his career the same year that George Jackson went to prison.
sentences.zh: 他开始职业生涯的那一年正是乔治·杰克逊入狱的那一年。

sentences.en: I understand you interviewed Carl Larson,
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你采访了卡尔·拉尔森，

sentences.en: and his view gives us a glimpse into the other side of the story,
sentences.zh: 他的观点让我们得以一窥故事的另一面，

sentences.en: how prison guards and prison officials see the need for solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 即狱警和监狱官员如何看待对单独监禁的需求。

sentences.en: So Carl Larson was one of the earlier people I interviewed in doing this work,
sentences.zh: 所以卡尔·拉尔森是我在做这项工作时较早采访的人之一，

sentences.en: and to my surprise, we got to be friends.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，我们成了朋友。

sentences.en: I came at this work from a perspective of a prisoner's rights advocate,
sentences.zh: 我开展这项工作时带着囚犯权益活动人士的视角，

sentences.en: very critical of the system.
sentences.zh: 对这个体制持极度批评的态度。

sentences.en: But as I got to know Carl Larson,
sentences.zh: 但随着我对卡尔·拉尔森的了解加深，

sentences.en: I saw that he had a really interesting perspective on the system,
sentences.zh: 我发现他对这个体制有着非常有趣的看法，

sentences.en: and he was one of the first people to point me to the story of George Jackson,
sentences.zh: 他是最早向我指出乔治·杰克逊故事的人之一，

sentences.en: and to explain how scary it was to be a guard working in the California prisons in the 1970s
sentences.zh: 并向我解释了在20世纪70年代这些命案发生时，

sentences.en: when these deaths were happening,
sentences.zh: 在加州监狱工作的狱警有多么恐惧，

sentences.en: and to make that fear real for me in a way that helped me to understand
sentences.zh: 他让我真切地感受到了那种恐惧，这帮我理解了

sentences.en: why he thought a long-term solitary confinement facility made sense.
sentences.zh: 为什么他认为长期单独监禁设施是合理的。

sentences.en: So Carl Larson is particularly interesting because, as you said,
sentences.zh: 所以卡尔·拉尔森特别有趣，因为正如你所说，

sentences.en: he started out as an officer in the 1970s in California prisons,
sentences.zh: 他从20世纪70年代起就是加州监狱的一名警官，

sentences.en: actually even earlier,
sentences.zh: 实际上甚至更早，

sentences.en: and then he worked his way up through the system, becoming a warden,
sentences.zh: 然后他在体制内步步高升，成为了一名典狱长，

sentences.en: and then becoming head of the prison construction projects that California engaged in in the 1980s
sentences.zh: 后来又成为了加州在20世纪80年代进行的监狱建设项目的负责人，

sentences.en: when the state built one of these long-term solitary confinement supermax facilities.
sentences.zh: 当时该州建造了这些长期单独监禁的超级最高安全级别设施之一。

sentences.en: And he takes credit for designing one of the first of these institutions,
sentences.zh: 他因设计了其中第一批机构而居功至伟，

sentences.en: and that's really interesting because he's a prison administrator.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣，因为他是一名监狱管理者。

sentences.en: He's not an architect.
sentences.zh: 他不是建筑师。

sentences.en: He's not an expert in exactly what kinds of punishments work.
sentences.zh: 他不是关于究竟哪种惩罚管用的专家。

sentences.en: He didn't have a law degree.
sentences.zh: 他没有法学学位。

sentences.en: He had just worked in prisons, and he designed this completely new facility.
sentences.zh: 他只是在监狱里工作过，然后他设计了这个全新的设施。

sentences.en: I understand that there were some interesting architectural features of this facility, Pelican Bay.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，这个名为鹈鹕湾的设施有一些有趣的建筑特色。

sentences.en: The cement for the facility was poured in one large block
sentences.zh: 该设施的水泥是一大块整体浇筑的，

sentences.en: so that the cells were not built in individual units?
sentences.zh: 所以牢房不是在单独的单元里建造的吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So one of the things that's striking about the place is it's made of these poured concrete cells,
sentences.zh: 所以这个地方引人注目的特点之一是它由这些浇筑的混凝土牢房组成，

sentences.en: so they're incredibly easy to hose down,
sentences.zh: 因此它们极其容易用水管冲洗，

sentences.en: which is the fact that they can stay clean is important
sentences.zh: 能够保持清洁这一点很重要，

sentences.en: because courts earlier had criticized isolation units for being really dirty.
sentences.zh: 因为此前法院曾批评隔离区非常脏。

sentences.en: And they're grouped together into these pods of eight,
sentences.zh: 它们被组合成每八个一组的舱，

sentences.en: and then the pods of eight are grouped together again into these tessellated T structures
sentences.zh: 然后这些八人舱又再次组合成这些镶嵌的T形结构，

sentences.en: so that one officer can look out over six pods of cells at a time.
sentences.zh: 这样一名警官一次就可以俯瞰六个牢房舱。

sentences.en: So it's a modern panopticon,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个现代的圆形监狱，

sentences.en: and that also allows the fact that there are no windows
sentences.zh: 这也使得没有窗户这一事实

sentences.en: makes it really easy to just fit all these blocks together
sentences.zh: 变得很容易将所有这些方块拼合在一起，

sentences.en: if you can imagine that structure.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象出那个结构的话。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, Karamit, if you can actually just describe
sentences.zh: 卡拉米特，我想知道你是否能直接描述一下

sentences.en: what one of these cells looks like.
sentences.zh: 其中一个牢房是什么样子的。

sentences.en: Give me a sense of what's in the cell, how big it is.
sentences.zh: 让我对牢房里的东西、它有多大有个概念。

sentences.en: What does it actually feel like to be in one of these units?
sentences.zh: 身处其中到底是什么感觉？

sentences.en: So the cells in these units are generally about 8 by 10 feet.
sentences.zh: 所以这些单元里的牢房通常大约是8乘10英尺。

sentences.en: So imagine a wheelchair-accessible bathroom stall or a generous parking space.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下无障碍卫生间隔间或者宽敞的停车位。

sentences.en: Pretty small.
sentences.zh: 相当小。

sentences.en: You can almost reach from one end of the cell to the other.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以从牢房的一端够到另一端。

sentences.en: And they're fairly self-contained.
sentences.zh: 而且它们相当独立完备。

sentences.en: So they contain a poured concrete ledge with a very thin piece of foam over it,
sentences.zh: 所以它们包含一个浇筑的混凝土台阶，上面铺着一层非常薄的泡沫垫，

sentences.en: and that's the bed.
sentences.zh: 那就是床。

sentences.en: And then there's another sort of concrete bit protruding
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一个突出的混凝土结构，

sentences.en: that is a desk and seat combination.
sentences.zh: 是一个书桌和座位的组合。

sentences.en: So it's just like a concrete block that a prisoner could sit on and write there.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像一个混凝土块，囚犯可以坐在上面并在那里写字。

sentences.en: And then in another corner, there's a steel, usually toilet-sink combination.
sentences.zh: 然后在另一个角落，有一个通常是钢铁材质的马桶洗手池组合。

sentences.en: So it's just one smooth steel object that has running water and plumbing for the prisoner.
sentences.zh: 所以它只是一个光滑的钢铁物件，为囚犯提供自来水和管道设施。

sentences.en: Sometimes there are showers in these cells,
sentences.zh: 有时这些牢房里有淋浴间，

sentences.en: but generally it's just a sink and a toilet.
sentences.zh: 但通常只有一个洗手池和一个马桶。

sentences.en: And again, if the prisoner is lucky and they can afford it
sentences.zh: 再说一次，如果囚犯很幸运，他们负担得起，

sentences.en: and the system they're in allows it, they might have a TV or a radio.
sentences.zh: 并且他们所在的体制允许，他们可能会有一台电视或收音机。

sentences.en: And usually they're allowed maybe a few books at a time
sentences.zh: 通常他们一次只能被允许带几本书

sentences.en: and a little bit of paper for writing letters or doing legal paperwork.
sentences.zh: 以及一点用来写信或处理法律文件的纸张。

sentences.en: You say in the book that despite what prison officials say,
sentences.zh: 你在书中提到，尽管监狱官员这么说，

sentences.en: it's not always the worst of the worst who end up in solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 但最终被单独监禁的并不总是罪大恶极的人。

sentences.en: But in general, are there patterns to predict who ends up in solitary confinement?
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，有没有什么规律可以预测谁最终会被单独监禁？

sentences.en: There's been shockingly little research over time on who ends up in solitary confinement and how.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，随着时间的推移，关于谁以及如何被单独监禁的研究少之又少。

sentences.en: And it's very hard to track across states.
sentences.zh: 而且很难在各州之间进行追踪。

sentences.en: But as people have paid more attention to this and through the work I've done,
sentences.zh: 但随着人们对此给予更多关注以及通过我所做的工作，

sentences.en: I've started to see some patterns.
sentences.zh: 我开始看到一些规律。

sentences.en: There's a disproportionate racial impact of solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 单独监禁具有不成比例的种族影响。

sentences.en: So we know that in our prisons in general,
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，在我们总体的监狱中，

sentences.en: African-Americans and Latinos are more likely to be in prison than in the general prison population.
sentences.zh: 与普通犯人群体相比，非裔美国人和拉丁裔美国人更容易身处监狱之中。

sentences.en: And they're doubly likely, again, to be in solitary confinement than even the general prison population.
sentences.zh: 而且，与普通犯人群体相比，他们被单独关押的可能性甚至会翻倍。

sentences.en: And that's often because gang members are being targeted for long-term isolation,
sentences.zh: 这通常是因为帮派成员成为长期隔离的目标，

sentences.en: especially in states like California.
sentences.zh: 特别是在像加利福尼亚这样的州。

sentences.en: into their 40s and 50s.

sentences.zh: 所以你的书出版之际，许多自由派和保守派携手呼吁

sentences.en: confinement is very, very expensive.

sentences.zh: 而把一个人关在隔离区，

sentences.en: or getting them a meal.

sentences.zh: 这甚至还没有被包含在
